_note: Player tips (ROADMAP M4 session 33). Each tip shows at its moment until the player closes it with "Don't show this message again" ticked (round 23), while the player's "Show player tips" option is on; those are remembered in the options, not the save. moment: where the game asks for a tip (edit_units_open: Edit Units opens; map_open: the map shows with nothing over it, after the opening Edit Units, or at the start of a Quick start game; encounter_open: the encounter dialog before a fight shows; squad_menu_open: a squad's menu opens; time_started: time first runs in a game (the player unpauses); battle_over: a battle's results show; battle_open: the battle view has opened, waiting for Play (round 24); fight_started: a battle begins playing (the tip pauses it, its controls showing); town_liberated, tower_liberated: the liberation window for one opens; neutral_met: the window for meeting a neutral band opens, Recruit, Fight or Sneak past; base_in_view: time is running and the Player Base is on screen; portal_ready: you hold two temples at once for the first time, so the Portal can be used (round 19); squad_stopped: a squad of yours stops on the map somewhere that is not a building to liberate (round 21); move_planning: you start laying a squad's move (not a deploy); shop_open: a shop opens; heal_open: the Heal window opens (round 23); after:<id>: the tip <id> has just been closed, the next tip following on from it). anchor: the part of the screen the popup points at (center: none, the tip sits in the middle of the screen with no arrow; recruit_pool: the Recruits list in Edit Units; deploy_button: the toolbar's Deploy Squad; garrison_town: the town Quick start's Garrison holds, on the map, framed with your base first; panel: the liberation window, the encounter dialog or the neutral band's window; actions: the squad menu's row of buttons; results: the end-of-battle panel; tactic: the battle's Tactic menu; play: the battle's Fight/Play button; speed: the game speed menu under the minimap; leader_squad: the Opinion Leader's squad card in Edit Units; player_base: the Player Base, on the map; squad_drawer: the squad list at the left of the map; followable: an enemy or neutral squad on the move, on screen, that can be followed). needs: a fact the tip waits for (flyer: the army has a flying unit; enemy:<class>: that class is in the enemy squad of the battle under way; defeat_leader, defeat_base: that defeat is on for this map; followable: such a squad is on screen; home_ground: someone in the coming fight is on their home terrain, or on rough ground away from it). modes: game modes it shows in (single_map, campaign, quick_start); missing means all. {town} in a tip's text is the Garrison's town; {leader} is the Opinion Leader's name. Tips are offered in this order.

edit_units_intro.text: This is the Edit Units screen. Here you can arrange your squads prior to their deployment. By default, your initial squads are assembled for you but feel free to optimize them as you see fit. When you are ready, click the Done button in the top right to enter the main map view.

opinion_leader.text: This is your Opinion Leader's squad. If your Opinion Leader, {leader}, falls, you lose this engagement.

build_squad.text: To begin creating a new squad, drag a leader into an empty slot. To add to a squad, drag any unit into an active squad slot.

flyers.text: You have a flying unit. Flyers can't take buildings: a squad needs at least one unit on foot to liberate a town, tower or temple.

march.text: The enemy's Garrison holds {town}, close to your base. Click your squad at the Player Base to open its menu, choose Move (the footprints), then click {town} twice to send it there. Press Space to start time.

deploy.text: Use the deploy button to send your squads out into the field of battle after composing them in the edit units screen. Conquering buildings will provide bonuses and abilities.

first_battle.text: A fight is about to begin. Heal uses herbs and Revival Draughts on this squad first. View Squad and Map pauses and puts this aside, so you can shop, heal, change the formation (Edit squad) or move other squads; it comes back when you resume. Begin Battle opens the battle, where you choose a tactic and press Fight.

first_town.text: Your reputation will rise if you liberate towns with positively aligned characters. Towns that you control at the end of the day cycle will provide income to help your empire thrive. Some towns also feature shops, indicated by a dollar symbol on the roof of their icon.

first_tower.text: Your reputation will rise if you liberate towers with negatively aligned characters. Towers that you control at the end of the day cycle will provide income to help your armies grow in power. Some towers also feature shops.

squad_menu.text: A squad's orders: edit it, heal it (the red cross), shop, move, or send it home. Hover over a button to see what it does, or why it's greyed out.

healing.text: Hurt or fallen units can be healed: open the squad's menu and press Heal (the red cross) to use Herbs and Revival Draughts anywhere, or stand in a temple to pay for healing and reviving there.

battle_controls.text:
To begin the battle, press play or use the space bar.

You can pause again any time in order to view the game log, play tarot cards, and adjust the game speed and squad tactics.

tactics.text: Note: Some squads require different tactics than others. Try switching your squad's tactics to leader here.

time_controls.text:
You can use this menu to adjust the speed of the game and to pause it.

Alternatively, you can use PgUp and PgDn to adjust speed up and down and hit the space bar to pause and resume.

The 'skip to action' button beside it advances the game until one of your squads encounters an interruption in their current status, such as an arrival at a destination, a battle, or an encounter with a neutral party.

neutral_met.text: In the course of your travels, you will encounter unallied units. These groups might be persuaded to join your cause, or they might prove violent. It is up to you whether to try and engage or to do your best to avoid them. Be warned - neutral parties can vary in power greatly, and can prove to be a great asset or a source of great pain to your army.

portal.text: Temples are not only places of worship; they contain portals that connect the land. When you control a temple, you can teleport instantly to any other temple you hold.

home_base.text: This is your home base. Defend it with your strongest soldiers, for if it falls, you lose this engagement.

follow.text: Want to keep an enemy from getting away? Set your squad to follow them by clicking on them as a move destination.

shop.text: Welcome to the shop. You can buy potions and equipment here to aid your army's conquest. You can also sell items when you are short on cash or just feeling greedy. Items sell for half of their original cost so plan carefully.

heal.text: When your squad has taken damage, you can heal and revive them on the heal screen. This will always be available anytime on the map or before a fight. Make sure to keep your army stocked with potions or you'll have nothing to heal with soon enough!

terrain.text:
Every unit has a home terrain that gives them an offensive and defensive bonus as well as a movement bonus on the map.

You can find a unit's terrain preference by inspecting it.

A squad's terrain preference is determined by the units that make it up. So be strategic in your squad composition to take advantage of terrain types.

squad_drawer.text:
It's easy to lose track of which squads are in motion, which are stationary, and where they are.

You can use the left hand menu to find each deployed squad, and double clicking on a squad brings up its menu. Each squad has an icon indicating whether it is stationary or in motion.

The control at the top of the menu expands and contracts its content.
